name: Rabat Medina
hero_subtitle: Compact historic lanes, Rue des Consuls and souks between the kasbah and the ocean walls.

overview.title: A medina you can actually finish
overview.p1: Rabat’s medina is smaller and flatter than Fez or Marrakech. You can cross it without a guide, browse carpet and craft shops on Rue des Consuls, and step out toward the ocean walls or up to the Udayas. It feels lived-in rather than purely theatrical.
overview.p2: Mornings bring market energy; evenings suit a slow dinner. Keep valuables close in busy lanes.

food.title: Eating in the medina
food.p1: Le Dinarjat and Dar Naji are classic addresses. Simple grills and juice stalls fill the gaps.
food.p2: Book popular houses in advance at weekends.
food.li5: Seafood if you walk toward the ocean.

1.title: Orientation
1.desc: Udayas gate and Avenue Hassan II help you reset if you turn corners.

2.title: Shopping
2.desc: Light bargaining on crafts; fixed prices on many everyday goods.

3.title: Evening
3.desc: Stick to busier lanes after dark.

q1.question: Do I need a guide?
q1.answer: Not for a basic walk — the medina is compact.

q2.question: Main shopping street?
q2.answer: Rue des Consuls is the best known for crafts.

q3.question: Distance to Udayas?
q3.answer: Short uphill walk to the kasbah gate.

q5.question: Best for first-timers?
q5.answer: Yes — a gentle introduction to Moroccan medinas.
